newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, awaiting foreign buyers.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, awaiting foreign buyers.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.84 percent on Thursday, the third straight day of losses, and traders said there was little sign of a recovery while foreign investors held back.
"Prices will remain low until foreign investors return to the market, which may last a couple of weeks. When they are back, the rising trend will start again," said Goran Spasenic of brokerage BPH.
The central bank last week said international investors have to open custody accounts at any of Slovenia's 14 fully licenced banks in order to trade in Slovenia's securities.
The bank later defended its move as purely regulating foreign portfolio investment not blocking it, but commercial banks said it would take them two to three weeks to prepare custody accounts.
"Due to the unexpected central bank action foreigners may be more cautious when dealing with Slovenian shares in the future but they still show a lot of interest in securities," an analyst said.
He forecast fresh capital would continue to flow into the market but not at the rate seen at the start of the year.
The Bank of Slovenia estimated foreigners invested some $30 million in Slovenian securities in the first six weeks of 1997, compared to 71 million in the whole of 1996.
The SBI index fell 26.26 points to 1,404.06. Since Tuesday the blue-chip index has fallen 4.31 percent.
Turnover rose to 315.1 million from 235.3 million. Overall eight shares fell, five rose and four were unchanged, while eight were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 3.44 percent to 58,900 tolars on volume of 2,742 shares for total turnover of 165.1 million tolars.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 8.45 percent to 6,500 tolars on volume of 228 shares for total turnover of 1.5 million tolars.
Preferred shares of trading company Kovinotehna were the biggest gainers, jumping 9.40 percent to 547 tolars on volume of one share. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
